suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-23 adds this relationship only as a bounded cutaneous premalignant-lesion association. The cited systematic review evaluates the natural history of actinic keratosis and progression or regression patterns, but it does not establish that any individual's squamous-cell carcinoma arose from an actinic keratosis or exclude field cancerization, cumulative ultraviolet exposure, immunosuppression, genetic susceptibility, prior lesions, or other causes. Require clinically or biopsy-documented actinic keratosis, separately established cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma, compatible anatomic site and chronology, and pathology/dermatology review. Do not infer carcinoma from an actinic keratosis diagnosis, lesion appearance, dysplasia, or treatment history alone.
evidenceGaps: Independent dermatologic or pathology documentation of actinic keratosis and cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma
Biopsy reports identifying carcinoma, anatomic site, margins, and relevant histopathology
Chronology of lesion recognition, persistence, progression, biopsy, treatment, recurrence, and cancer diagnosis
Assessment of ultraviolet exposure, field cancerization, immunosuppression, prior skin cancers, phenotype, and other risk factors

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented actinic keratosis and cutaneous SCC with compatible site/chronology and pathology review; do not infer carcinoma from a lesion or treatment history alone.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited systematic review supports review of actinic keratosis as a premalignant cutaneous lesion with variable progression and regression, without establishing deterministic individual origin of every later squamous-cell carcinoma.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; pathology, anatomic site, chronology, dermatologic findings, and competing risk factors are required for individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Actinic keratosis and cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma may share ultraviolet-related field damage and clonal keratinocyte changes, but the individual lesion-to-carcinoma pathway remains hypothesized until pathology, site, chronology, and competing risk factors are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The cited review addresses actinic-keratosis natural history but does not prove that a particular cutaneous SCC arose from a documented actinic keratosis; pathology, chronology, site, and other skin-cancer risks require review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent lesion and carcinoma pathology; compatible anatomic site and chronology; dermatology records; ultraviolet and immunosuppression history; prior skin cancer history; and assessment of field cancerization and other competing explanations.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: cumulative ultraviolet exposure and field cancerization
